## rb_midpoint: a note on the implementation

The original implementation (in rb_grade) used:

```r
x %/% dx * dx + dx / 2
```

This is concise and correct for most inputs, but fails silently when `dx` is a
value that cannot be represented exactly in IEEE 754 floating-point — for
example `0.1`. In those cases `0.3 / 0.1` evaluates to `2.9999...` rather than
`3`, so `%/%` floors to `2` instead of `3`, placing the value in the wrong bin:

```r
0.3 %/% 0.1 * 0.1 + 0.05  # returns 0.25, expected 0.35
```

The fix is to round the ratio before flooring, which corrects the floating-point
noise before it affects the result:

```r
floor(round(x / dx, digits = 10)) * dx + dx / 2
```

The precision of 10 decimal places is conservative: it is tight enough to
correct the representation error in `0.3 / 0.1` (~1e-15) while being far too
coarse to accidentally collapse genuinely distinct values.

### DuckDB / duckdbfs

`rb_midpoint()` includes a dbplyr SQL translation, so it works transparently in
`mutate()` on DuckDB-backed tables — including those opened with
`duckdbfs::open_dataset()`:

```r
library(dplyr)
library(duckdbfs)

open_dataset("catch.parquet") |>
  mutate(lon_bin = rb_midpoint(lon, dx = 0.5),
         lat_bin = rb_midpoint(lat, dx = 0.5))
```

The generated SQL uses `FLOOR(ROUND(x / dx, 10)) * dx + dx / 2`, which handles
floating-point bin widths (e.g. `0.1`) correctly in DuckDB.
